RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of bias is professionally counterproductive and legally baseless. An all-female panel alone does not indicate discrimination. 

For a "head of" position, banks heavily prioritize regulatory affairs expertise, governance, and executive stakeholder management alongside technical ability. The selected candidate’s regulatory background is a standard, highly legitimate rationale for hiring at that leadership level over purely academic or technical depth. 

Making an unsubstantiated accusation of bias will burn professional bridges within the institution and the broader industry. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on your interviews to identify areas to strengthen for future executive roles.
